newsitem.title: UK: Work conditions Labour's poison pill - UK's Major.
newsitem.headline: Work conditions Labour's poison pill - UK's Major.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major on Tuesday said there was a "poison pill" in the opposition Labour Party's plans to accept European Union legislation on working conditions.
Major was speaking at the penultimate session of Prime Minister's Question time before the May 1 general election, and on the eve of the publication of a new set of unemployment figures.
He told MPs: "We intend to continue to put people back to work as we have done in spectacular fashion in the last 18 months."

Major added: "Policies like the Social Chapter, the minimum wage, the 48 hour week, however glib they may sound, are a recipe for putting people out of work if they are in work, and if they are out of work making sure they stay out of work for a long time ahead."
"That is the poison pill of the opposition policy," he added.
